business_problem: Xiangnong Technology needed a cost-effective but production-grade AI stack for Chinese NLP products that span writing assistance, document intelligence, public-opinion analysis, and government workflows. As a fast-growing startup, it could not afford to run its own datacenter, yet it still needed large-scale GPU training capacity, low-cost storage for massive text corpora, faster preprocessing, and stable monitoring as it turned research-led language models into enterprise services.
solution_summary: Xiangnong Technology built its Chinese NLP platform on Alibaba Cloud instead of operating its own machine room. The company first moved workloads to Elastic Compute Service and self-managed Kubernetes, then adopted AKS as the business expanded so containerized model services could scale with less operations overhead. For deep-learning training and inference, Xiangnong uses GPU and AMD instances, with Object Storage Service acting as the shared corpus and artifact layer for large training sets. EMR handles preprocessing and analytics on raw language data before jobs are scheduled into the cloud AI system, while Cloud Monitor watches GPU utilization and alerts on runtime anomalies. Load balancing, autoscaling, and orchestration complete the delivery path so the same stack can support FireDragon Writing, intelligent document processing, smart Q&A engines, public-opinion monitoring, and public-sector applications such as the Yuhang District People's Congress suggestion-routing platform.

solution_components.name: GPU instances
solution_components.role: Provide the accelerated training and inference capacity for Xiangnong's deep-learning NLP workloads.

solution_components.name: AMD instances
solution_components.role: Expand the compute pool for model training and other high-volume AI tasks that do not require the same GPU profile.

solution_components.name: Object Storage Service (OSS)
solution_components.role: Stores large training corpora, intermediate datasets, and model artifacts at low cost.

solution_components.name: EMR
solution_components.role: Preprocesses and analyzes large text datasets before they are used by Xiangnong's NLP models.

solution_components.name: Elastic Compute Service (ECS)
solution_components.role: Runs the core cloud hosts that support training jobs and production NLP services.

solution_components.name: AKS
solution_components.role: Orchestrates containerized NLP services and reduces the operations burden of scaling the AI platform.

solution_components.name: Cloud Monitor
solution_components.role: Tracks GPU resources and service health so the team can keep the AI platform stable and secure.

data_flow: Enterprise text, public-opinion, and domain datasets are stored in OSS, preprocessed in EMR, and then fed into GPU and AMD training jobs running on ECS and AKS. The trained models are exposed through load-balanced application services that power writing assistance, document processing, smart Q&A, and public-sector routing workflows, while Cloud Monitor feeds alerts and capacity signals back to the operations team.
business_outcome: Alibaba Cloud gave Xiangnong Technology a foundation that could turn Chinese NLP research into production services. The company scaled a portfolio covering writing assistance, intelligent document processing, smart Q&A, and public-sector workflow automation; grew FireDragon Writing registrations by 1500% in one year; and delivered a Yuhang District People's Congress suggestion-routing platform that cut a task from 3 minutes to 0.35 seconds and reduced total handling time from 8 hours to 5 minutes while keeping accuracy above 90%.

architecture_clues: The platform combines OSS for low-cost corpus storage with EMR preprocessing before training workloads run on GPU and AMD instances.
Xiangnong evolved from self-managed Kubernetes on ECS to AKS as the NLP service footprint expanded.
Cloud Monitor is used specifically for GPU monitoring and alerting rather than only generic host telemetry.
The same cloud AI stack supports consumer writing assistants, enterprise knowledge workflows, and public-sector routing systems.
